source.title: LLM Unlearning Under the Microscope: A Full-Stack View on Methods and Metrics
source.authors: Chong-Yu Fan; Chang-Sheng Wang; Yan-Chen Huang; Soumyadeep Pal; Si-Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests unlearning effectiveness and robustness, including GCG jailbreak attacks, but does not test whether safety-trained models lose refusal behavior after fine-tuning or whether safety differences concentrate in early response tokens.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GCG jailbreak results for WMDP unlearning, but its outcome is WMDP accuracy, not refusal or harmful-completion rates; those results are recorded under fits_no_version. It reports no fine-tuning-on-benign-or-harmful-safety-examples test, per-token KL measurement, parameter localization test, or safety-deepening experiment.
record.test_reason: This is a machine-unlearning study on WMDP-Bio with Llama-3 8B Instruct. Every outcome is hazardous-knowledge accuracy (MCQ) or an entailment score, never a refusal or harmful-compliance rate of a safety-trained model. Its attacks are GCG jailbreaks, relearning on forget data, benign out-of-domain fine-tuning and quantization. They resemble V1, V2 and V4 but measure whether removed knowledge returns, not whether safety refusal is lost. There is no per-token KL, no parameter localization of safety and no safety-deepening test. Qi et al. (2023) appears only as a related-work citation, so the study does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The authors also conclude that MCQ-only evaluation overstates unlearning success, and that divergence-driven methods over-forget and damage generation. They add that relearning and out-of-domain fine-tuning are distinct robustness axes: divergence methods resist relearning, representation methods resist fine-tuning. Jailbreak robustness tracks relearning robustness, and robust designs (SAM, IRM, TAR, but not RMU+LAT) generally improve resilience.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates machine-unlearning methods, not the safety fine-tuning or token-position methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported WMDP jailbreak robustness varies across unlearning methods; the authors say robust designs generally improve it, with RMU+LAT as an exception. They also report that robustness patterns differ across in-domain relearning and out-of-domain fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Under enhanced GCG, WMDP MCQ accuracy of unlearned models rises from about 0.27–0.33 to 0.38–0.68 depending on method. Exceptions are IDK+AP (0.32→0.29), NPO+SAM, NPO+IRM and TAR, which barely move. RMU (0.59) and ELM (0.68) recover most knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-level jailbreaks recover unlearned hazardous knowledge to a degree that depends on the unlearning method family.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign out-of-domain fine-tuning (GSM8K, SST-2, MNLI; 250 steps) and in-domain relearning (100 steps on forget data) both raise WMDP accuracy and ES of unlearned models (Fig. 2). Relearning is the worst case, e.g. RMU 0.27→0.70 MCQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned hazardous knowledge re-emerges after small amounts of fine-tuning, including on unrelated benign data.

record.problems: The experiments use Llama-3 8B Instruct for the reported comparisons, and the authors note that their evaluation relies heavily on automatic metrics, which may miss subtle behavior. The reported jailbreak outcome is WMDP answer-selection accuracy rather than a refusal-rate measure.

untested.parts: Not tested. Relearning on forget data restores WMDP knowledge accuracy, but no refusal or harmful-compliance rate is measured.
Not tested. Benign fine-tuning on GSM8K, SST-2 and MNLI raises WMDP accuracy, but no refusal or harmful-compliance rate is measured.
Not tested. GCG suffixes are applied to unlearned models and scored by WMDP MCQ accuracy, not refusal; there is no prefilling or decoding attack.
Not tested. Robust unlearning designs (SAM, IRM, TAR, LAT) are evaluated for knowledge-recovery resistance, not for deepening safety refusal.

missing.what: In-domain relearning, out-of-domain fine-tuning (GSM8K/SST-2/MNLI) and quantization results for all 12 methods, by MCQ accuracy and ES. These are the closest analogues to V1/V2 but measure knowledge recovery, not refusal.
missing.locator: Figure 2(a)(b); Figure 4(a) RobReL/RobFT/RobQT columns; Table A2

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only': Qi et al. is only cited in related work. Row values and baselines match the Fig. 4(a) Unlearned and RobJA columns. The Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 'unlearned' values for DPO and IDK+AP are swapped (0.32/0.33), a minor inconsistency in the paper. All rows correctly carry versions none.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests GCG attacks on unlearned WMDP knowledge, not whether compliant prefixes, suffixes, or decoding changes defeat refusal behavior.
